generated.description: The paragraph describing Krusche et al.'s interactive learning concept spans approximately 14-16 rendered lines, well exceeding the 10-line maximum. It also covers multiple distinct ideas: (1) adopting CI for learning, (2) shortening the theory-practice gap, (3) transfer of skills to use cases, (4) splitting the lecture into iterations, (5) describing the phases in detail, and (6) the subsequent building of Artemis. This paragraph should be split into at least 2-3 paragraphs of 5-8 lines each, with one coherent idea per paragraph.

locations.quote: In their paper Interactive Learning – Increasing Student Participation through Shorter Exercise Cycles, Krusche et al. have taken up this concept to improve the learning experience in large computer science courses at university [Krusche17]. They introduced an newly developed learning method which shortens the time between theory, which is usually taught in the non-interactive lecture, and practice, which typically follows about a week later, so that less knowledge is lost [Krusche17]. The concept, called Interactive learning, makes it possible for students to transfer the new acquired skills to real, application-based use cases still during lecture [Krusche17]. In order to implement this idea, the lecture is split up into multiple iterations, each consisting of different phases [Krusche17]. First there is a theory phase, before the instructor shows an example to the students. After that the students can try out the concept themselves, before they get a sample solution and instant, but still individual feedback generated by the CI server. Afterwards it is possible to reflect about the newly learned approach. With this fundamental idea, later the assessment management system Artemis was built [Krusche18].
